provenance.source: AI-drafted from general automotive knowledge (2026-10-06). Conceptual; not reviewed by a person; no manufacturer data.

problems.name: Engine overheating
problems.description: The engine is running hotter than its cooling system can control. Continuing to drive can warp the cylinder head and destroy the head gasket.
symptoms: Temperature gauge above its normal position or a red warning
Steam or a sweet smell from the bonnet
safety: Stop as soon as it is safe and switch the engine off.
Never open the coolant cap while the engine is hot: the coolant is under pressure and can scald.
checks: Once fully cold, check the coolant level.
Note when it happens: in traffic, at speed, under load, or all the time. Each points to a different cause.

problems.name: Coolant loss
problems.description: The coolant level keeps falling. A sealed cooling system should hardly lose any, so a falling level means it is going somewhere: outside, into the cabin, or into the engine.
symptoms: Puddle or crust under the bonnet
safety: Only open the cap with the engine cold.
Coolant is poisonous and tastes sweet: keep it away from children and animals.
checks: Mark the level cold and check again after a few drives to judge how fast it falls.
Look for where it goes: the ground, the engine, the carpets, the exhaust.

problems.name: Loss of power
problems.description: The vehicle does not accelerate as it should. The drive system needs air, fuel and spark (or battery power) in the right amounts, a free exhaust and a transmission that passes the power on; a shortfall in any of them shows as lost power.
symptoms: Slow to accelerate or to climb hills
A warning light or reduced-power message
Unusual noise or smoke under acceleration
safety: A sudden loss of power in traffic is a hazard: move out of the traffic flow before investigating.
checks: Is a warning light on? Stored fault codes are the quickest pointer.
Is it constant, or does it come and go? Does a restart cure it for a while?

problems.name: Hard starting or will not start
aliases: takes a long time to start
turns over but won t start
turns over but does not start
problems.description: The engine is slow to fire or does not fire at all. To start it needs to be turned fast enough, and to get fuel, air and ignition at the right moment.
symptoms: Normal cranking that goes on for a long time
safety: Do not crank for long periods: it overheats the starter and can flood the engine or the exhaust with fuel.
checks: Listen to the cranking: slow and laboured points at the battery or starter; normal speed points at fuel, ignition or a sensor.
Is it worse cold, hot, or after standing?

problems.name: Nothing happens or only clicks when starting
aliases: clicks when i turn the key
nothing happens when i turn the key
problems.description: The starter does not turn the engine at all: there is silence, a single click, or rapid clicking.
symptoms: Dashboard lights dim or go out
safety: If jump-starting, follow the handbook's connection order exactly.
checks: Do the dashboard and interior lights come on brightly? Do they dim when you try to start?

problems.name: Electric or hybrid car will not go READY
problems.description: The car does not switch into its drive-ready state. Before it closes the high-voltage contactors it needs a healthy 12 V supply, a recognised key, the brake pressed and a fault-free high-voltage system.
symptoms: Dashboard stays dark or shows a warning instead of READY
No click from under the car when switching on
safety: Never open or touch orange high-voltage cables or components.
checks: Is the charging cable still plugged in? Most cars will not go ready while connected.
Does the dashboard light up normally? A dark or flickering display points at the 12 V battery.

problems.name: Misfire or rough running
problems.description: One or more cylinders are not burning their fuel properly, so the engine runs unevenly.
symptoms: Engine warning light, flashing under load
safety: A flashing engine warning light means unburned fuel is reaching the catalytic converter: ease off and have it checked soon.
checks: Is it worse cold, hot, at idle or under load?
Have the fault codes read: they usually name the cylinder.

problems.name: Engine stalling or cutting out
problems.description: The engine stops by itself, at idle, when coming to a halt, or while driving.
symptoms: Stops when slowing to a halt
Cuts out when hot and restarts later
safety: If the engine stops while moving, steering and braking need much more effort: steer to safety and brake firmly.
checks: Does it happen hot or cold, at idle or at speed?
Does it restart at once, or only after cooling down?

problems.name: Engine warning light on
problems.description: The engine computer has stored a fault. The light alone says only that something is outside its expected range; the stored code says where to look.
safety: A flashing light, or a red one, means stop driving hard; a steady amber one means have it read soon.
checks: Have the fault codes read. Until then, the list below is only the commonest groups of causes.

problems.name: White exhaust smoke
problems.description: White exhaust is water vapour or, on a diesel, unburned fuel. A little vapour on a cold start is normal; thick, sweet-smelling white smoke from a warm engine is not.
symptoms: Thin vapour that clears as the engine warms (normal)
Thick white smoke with a sweet smell
safety: If the smoke is thick and the coolant level is dropping, stop driving: coolant in a cylinder can cause serious engine damage.
checks: Does it clear once the engine is warm?
Is the coolant level dropping?

problems.name: Blue exhaust smoke or oil consumption
problems.description: Blue-grey smoke is engine oil being burned. When it appears tells you where the oil gets in.
symptoms: Smoke after a long idle or overrun
safety: Keep checking the oil level: running low on oil destroys an engine quickly.
checks: When does it smoke: start-up (valve seals), acceleration (rings), under boost (turbo)?
How fast does the oil level fall?

problems.name: Black exhaust smoke
problems.description: Black smoke is soot: fuel burned with too little air. Either too much fuel is going in, or too little air.
checks: Is it under hard acceleration only, or all the time?

problems.name: High fuel consumption
problems.description: The car uses clearly more fuel than it used to for the same driving.
checks: Compare like with like: same route, season and load. Winter, short trips and roof loads all raise consumption with nothing wrong.

problems.name: Oil pressure warning
problems.description: The engine is warning that oil pressure is too low. Without pressure the bearings run metal on metal, and serious damage can follow within seconds.
symptoms: Warning that flickers at idle or in corners
safety: Stop and switch the engine off as soon as it is safe. Do not restart until the oil level has been checked.
checks: Check the oil level on level ground.
Listen: is the engine noisier than usual?

problems.name: Oil leak
problems.description: Engine oil is escaping to the outside. Small weeps are common on older engines; a leak that lowers the level between checks needs attention.
symptoms: Drips where the car is parked
safety: Oil on a hot exhaust can smoke and, rarely, ignite. Oil on tyres or brakes is dangerous.
checks: Place clean card under the engine overnight to see where it drips and how much.
Check the level regularly.

problems.name: Engine knocking, ticking or rattling
problems.description: A new rhythmic noise from the engine. Its pitch, and whether it follows engine speed or load, narrows down the source.
symptoms: Deep knock from low down that follows revs
safety: A deep knock that gets louder with revs means stop: continuing can wreck the engine.
checks: Check the oil level first.
Top or bottom of the engine? At idle, under load, or only for the first seconds?

problems.name: Loud or rattling exhaust
problems.description: The exhaust is louder than normal or rattles. Leaks before the silencers are loud; loose shields and broken internals rattle.
symptoms: Rattle at idle or one rev range
safety: An exhaust leak can let fumes into the cabin: drive with ventilation on fresh air and have it fixed.
checks: Where does it come from: front, middle or rear?

problems.name: Turbo whistle or siren noise
problems.description: A whistle, hiss or siren that rises with boost. A faint whistle can be normal; a new or much louder one usually means air is escaping or the turbo itself is wearing.
symptoms: Loss of power or smoke with it
safety: A turbo that is breaking up can send oil and debris into the engine: do not keep driving hard.
checks: Is there a loss of power or smoke as well?
Look at the boost hoses for splits and oily joints.

problems.name: DPF warning
problems.description: The diesel particulate filter is filling with soot faster than it can burn it off. Left alone it ends in reduced power and an expensive filter.
symptoms: Fan running after switch-off, higher idle
safety: Do not ignore the light: the longer the filter loads, the less likely it is to recover by itself.
checks: What kind of driving has the car done lately?
Are any other warning lights on?

problems.name: Battery or charging warning light
problems.description: The car is telling you the 12 V battery is not being charged. It will run on the battery alone until that is empty.
symptoms: Red battery symbol with the engine running
Other warnings appearing one after another
safety: Switch off what you can (heated screens, seats) and head somewhere safe: the engine will stop when the battery is empty.
checks: Is the auxiliary belt still there and turning?
Did the steering go heavy or the temperature rise at the same time? They can share the belt.

problems.name: Battery keeps going flat
problems.description: The 12 V battery is repeatedly too low to start the car. Either it can no longer hold a charge, it is not being charged, or something is emptying it.
symptoms: Needs a jump start after standing
checks: How old is the battery?
Does it go flat overnight, or only after a week or more?
What sort of journeys does the car do?

problems.name: Brake vibration
aliases: steering wheel shakes when i brake
steering wheel shaking when i brake
problems.description: The pedal pulses or the steering wheel shakes while braking. Braking force is varying as the wheel turns.
symptoms: Worse from high speed or when hot
safety: Braking distance can be longer. If it appeared suddenly or is severe, have it checked before driving at speed.
checks: Only when braking? Then it is in the brakes. At speed without braking? Look at wheels and tyres.
Felt in the steering wheel (front) or the seat (rear)?

problems.name: Brake squeal or grinding
problems.description: The brakes make noise. A light squeal can be harmless; grinding means metal is touching metal.
symptoms: Noise that stops or starts when the pedal is pressed
safety: Grinding means stop driving: the pads may be worn through and the discs are being destroyed.
checks: Does the noise happen while braking, or while not braking and stop when you brake?
Can you see pad material through the wheel?

problems.name: Soft or spongy brake pedal
aliases: brake pedal goes to the floor
problems.description: The pedal travels further than it should, feels soft, or sinks. The hydraulic system is not transmitting your foot's force properly.
safety: Do not drive with a soft or sinking pedal. Brakes can fail with little further warning.
checks: Check the brake fluid level.
Look for fluid inside the wheels and under the car.

problems.name: ABS or brake warning light
problems.description: The anti-lock or stability system has switched itself off after a fault, or the brake system is reporting low fluid or worn pads. Normal braking usually remains, without ABS.
symptoms: Traction or stability light with it
safety: A red brake warning means stop and check the fluid level. An amber ABS light means ordinary brakes still work, but wheels can lock in an emergency stop.
checks: Which lights exactly: amber ABS, red brake, or both?
Check the brake fluid level.

problems.name: Car pulls to one side
problems.description: The car does not hold a straight line by itself, either all the time or only when braking.
symptoms: Constant drift on a flat road
safety: A pull that appears suddenly, or under braking, needs checking before any fast driving.
checks: All the time, or only when braking? All the time points to tyres and alignment; braking points to a brake.
Road camber makes every car drift a little: test on a flat, empty road.

problems.name: Steering wheel vibration at speed
problems.description: The steering wheel or the whole car shakes at certain road speeds without the brakes being used.
symptoms: Felt in the wheel (front) or the seat (rear)
safety: A vibration that appears suddenly can mean a damaged tyre or loose wheel: stop and look before continuing.
checks: At what speed does it start and stop?
Look at each tyre for bulges and at each rim for a missing balance weight.

problems.name: Knocking or clunking over bumps
problems.description: Something in the suspension has developed play and knocks when the wheel moves.
symptoms: Clunk over speed humps or when braking
safety: Most knocks are wear, but a broken spring or failed ball joint is dangerous: have new noises checked.
checks: Front or rear, left or right?
Small bumps at low speed (links), big bumps (dampers, mounts), braking or pulling away (bushes)?

problems.name: Heavy steering
problems.description: Turning the wheel takes much more effort than usual, most of all at low speed.
safety: The car can still be steered without assistance, but it takes real effort: slow down and leave room.
checks: Did it happen suddenly, with a warning light?
Check the tyre pressures first.

problems.name: Humming or droning noise at speed
problems.description: A hum, drone or rumble that rises with road speed, whatever the engine is doing.
symptoms: Louder with speed, not with revs
safety: A badly worn wheel bearing can overheat or seize: do not leave a growing rumble.
checks: Does it change when you steer gently left and right? (bearing)
Does it change with the road surface? (tyres)
Does it change when you lift off the accelerator? (final drive)

problems.name: Clutch slipping
aliases: revs rise but the car does not accelerate
problems.description: The clutch does not grip fully: engine speed rises without the car accelerating to match.
safety: A slipping clutch gets worse quickly once it starts and can leave the car unable to move.
checks: In a high gear at low revs, accelerate firmly and watch the rev counter against the speed.

problems.name: Difficult or crunching gear change
problems.description: On a manual gearbox, gears are hard to select or crunch as they engage.
symptoms: Hard to select first or reverse at a standstill
checks: All gears, or one? One gear points inside the gearbox; all gears, especially from rest, points at the clutch not releasing.

problems.name: Automatic gearbox shifting badly
problems.description: An automatic or dual-clutch gearbox changes gear harshly, late, or lets the revs flare between gears.
safety: Continuing to drive a slipping automatic overheats and wears its clutches quickly.
checks: Cold only, hot only, or always?
Is a transmission warning showing?

problems.name: Clicking noise when turning
problems.description: A rhythmic click while turning under power, speeding up with the car.
safety: A CV joint that fails completely leaves that wheel without drive.
checks: In an empty car park, drive slowly in a tight circle each way and listen.
Look at the driveshaft boots behind the front wheels.

problems.name: Vibration when accelerating
problems.description: A shudder that appears while accelerating and eases when coasting. The parts that carry torque are the suspects.
checks: Does it stop the moment you lift off? Then it is torque-related, not wheel balance.

problems.name: Air conditioning not cold
problems.description: The air from the vents is not being cooled, or only slightly.
checks: Is the airflow strong but warm, or weak altogether?
Colder on the move than at a standstill?

problems.name: Heater not warm
problems.description: The cabin heater gives little or no heat.
safety: On a car with an engine, a heater that goes cold together with a rising temperature gauge means low coolant: stop and check once cold.
checks: Does the engine reach its normal temperature?
Check the coolant level cold.

problems.name: Reduced electric range
problems.description: The car goes less far on a charge than expected. Much of the variation is weather and speed; some is the battery ageing.
symptoms: Lower range estimate at full charge
Range falling faster than distance driven
checks: Compare like with like: same temperature, speed and route.
Check the tyre pressures.

problems.name: Will not charge or charges slowly
problems.description: The car does not start charging, stops early, or charges much more slowly than it should.
symptoms: Charging stops after a few minutes
Much lower power than the charger can give
safety: Never use a damaged cable or a connector that shows heat marks.
checks: Try another charger and cable first.
AC (home) or DC (rapid), or both? That separates the on-board charger from the battery.

causes.name: Low coolant level
causes.why: With too little coolant the pump cannot carry heat from the engine to the radiator, and air pockets form around the hottest parts.
signs: Level below MIN in the expansion tank when cold
Sweet smell or damp patches under the bonnet
checks: With the engine cold, compare the level in the expansion tank with its MIN and MAX marks.
Look for dried coolant (a white, pink or green crust) on hoses, the radiator and around the pump.

causes.name: Coolant hose or clamp leak
causes.why: Hoses harden and crack with heat and age, and clamps loosen. Coolant escapes fastest when the system is hot and under pressure.
signs: Drips or a crust at a hose joint
A swollen, soft or cracked hose
checks: With the engine cold, look along each hose and squeeze it: cracks, bulges and wet joints are the signs.

causes.name: Radiator leak
causes.why: Corrosion or stone damage opens the core, or the plastic end tanks split at their seams.
signs: Coolant under the front of the car
checks: Look at the radiator face and the seams of its end tanks for stains or wet patches.

causes.name: Water pump seal leak
causes.why: The shaft seal wears and coolant weeps from the pump body; a leaking pump is often followed by a failing bearing.
signs: A coolant trace below the pump
Grinding or whining from the pump area
checks: Look below the pump for a coolant trail or crust.

causes.name: Expansion tank or pressure cap fault
causes.why: The cap holds the system under pressure, which raises the boiling point. A weak cap lets coolant vent or boil off; a cracked tank leaks.
checks: With the engine cold, look at the cap seal and the tank for cracks and stains.

causes.name: Heater core leak
causes.why: The small radiator behind the dashboard can corrode through; the coolant then ends up inside the car.
signs: Windows mist up with a sweet smell
Damp carpet in a front footwell
checks: Feel the front carpets for dampness and notice any sweet smell from the vents.

causes.name: Head gasket failure
causes.why: The gasket seals combustion, coolant and oil between block and head. When it fails, combustion gas is pushed into the coolant, or coolant is drawn into a cylinder or the oil.
signs: Coolant level drops with no visible leak
A milky deposit under the oil filler cap
checks: Watch the expansion tank with the engine running: a steady stream of bubbles is a warning sign.
Look under the oil filler cap and at the dipstick for a milky emulsion.
A workshop can test the coolant for combustion gas.

causes.name: An earlier overheat
causes.why: One severe overheat can distort the head and damage the gasket. Whatever caused that overheat may still be there.
signs: The problem began after the temperature gauge went into the red
checks: Think back: did the engine overheat before these symptoms started?

causes.name: Warped or cracked cylinder head
causes.why: Heat distorts the head so the gasket can no longer seal, or cracks it between coolant passages and the combustion chamber.
checks: This needs the head removed and measured by a workshop.

causes.name: Thermostat stuck closed
causes.why: A thermostat that does not open keeps coolant circulating inside the engine only, so the radiator never gets the chance to cool it.
signs: Overheats within a few minutes of driving
One radiator hose stays much cooler than the engine
checks: Once warm, carefully compare the two radiator hoses: both should become hot. One staying cool points at the thermostat.

causes.name: Thermostat stuck open
causes.why: Coolant goes through the radiator all the time, so the engine takes very long to warm up or never reaches its normal temperature. A cold engine uses more fuel and heats the cabin poorly.
signs: Temperature gauge stays low, especially on the open road
checks: Watch the temperature gauge on a longer drive: it should reach its normal position and stay there.

causes.name: Water pump not circulating
causes.why: If the impeller is corroded or loose on its shaft, or the pump is not being driven, coolant stops moving and the heat stays in the engine.
signs: Heater goes cold as the gauge climbs
checks: Look at the belt that drives the pump (where it is visible) for glazing, cracks or slack.

causes.name: Worn or slipping pump impeller
causes.why: The impeller blades erode, or a plastic impeller comes loose on its shaft: the pump turns but moves little coolant.
signs: No leak and no noise, yet poor circulation

causes.name: Pump drive belt slipping or broken
causes.why: The pump is driven by the auxiliary belt or the timing drive. A slipping or broken belt stops it.
signs: Battery light at the same time (shared belt)
checks: Look at the auxiliary belt for cracks, glazing and tension.

causes.name: Radiator blocked
causes.why: Scale and sludge block the tubes inside, or leaves and insects block the fins outside; either way less heat is shed.
signs: Runs hot under load or in hot weather
Cold patches on the radiator face
checks: Look through the grille: are the fins packed with leaves, insects or dirt?

causes.name: Internal blockage (scale or sludge)
causes.why: Old or mixed coolant leaves deposits that narrow the tubes.
checks: Look at the coolant in the expansion tank: it should be clear and coloured, not brown or oily.

causes.name: Fins blocked or bent
causes.why: Air cannot pass through fins that are clogged with debris or flattened.
signs: Debris visible between condenser and radiator
checks: Look at the fins from the front for debris and flattened areas.

causes.name: Cooling fan not running
causes.why: At low speed there is little natural airflow, so the fan must pull air through the radiator. If it does not run, temperature climbs in traffic and falls again on the open road.
signs: Overheats in traffic or at idle, fine at speed
Fan never heard when the engine is hot
checks: With the engine fully warm and idling, listen for the fan cutting in. Keep hands clear: it can start at any time.

causes.name: Fan motor failed
causes.why: A worn or seized motor does not turn when it is powered.
signs: Fan blades stiff to turn by hand (engine off and cold)

causes.name: Fan relay, fuse or wiring
causes.why: The motor is fine but no power reaches it.
signs: Fan works on one speed only, or not at all
checks: Check the fan fuse in the fuse box against the diagram in the handbook.

causes.name: Temperature signal not reaching the fan control
causes.why: The fan is switched by the engine computer from the coolant temperature sensor. A wrong reading means it is never asked to run.
signs: Gauge reading does not match how hot the engine feels

causes.name: Air trapped in the cooling system
causes.why: An air pocket stops coolant reaching the pump, the heater or the sensor. It is common after the system has been opened or has run low.
checks: Was the cooling system opened or topped up recently? Air is likely afterwards.

causes.name: Faulty temperature reading
causes.why: The gauge and the engine computer rely on the sensor. A wrong reading can show overheating that is not happening, or hide overheating that is.
signs: Warning with no heat, steam or smell
checks: Note whether the gauge moves smoothly or jumps; a jump from normal to maximum in a second is rarely real heat.

causes.name: Heater core blocked
causes.why: Deposits narrow the small tubes of the heater core, so little hot coolant passes through it.
signs: Engine at normal temperature but the vents stay lukewarm
One side of the cabin warmer than the other

causes.name: Heater flap or climate control fault
causes.why: Flaps behind the dashboard mix hot and cold air. A failed flap motor or control leaves them in the wrong position.
signs: Temperature does not change when the dial is turned
checks: Turn the temperature from coldest to hottest and listen for the flap moving.

causes.name: Electric cabin heater or heat pump fault
causes.why: An electric car has no engine heat to borrow: an electric heater or heat pump warms the cabin. If it fails there is airflow but no heat.

causes.name: Clogged air filter
causes.why: A blocked filter limits how much air the engine can draw, so it cannot burn the fuel needed for full power.
signs: Filter element dark and packed with dirt
checks: Take the filter element out and hold it to the light: heavy dirt or oil means it is due.

causes.name: Turbocharger not making boost
causes.why: Without boost a turbocharged engine only receives the air a much smaller engine would, so power falls sharply. The engine computer may also cut power to protect itself.
checks: Listen for a new whistle or hiss under acceleration.
Look at the boost hoses and their clamps for splits and oily joints.

causes.name: Boost leak (hose, clamp or intercooler)
causes.why: Pressurised air escapes between the turbo and the engine, so less of it reaches the cylinders.
signs: An oily film around a hose joint
checks: Follow the pipework from turbo to intercooler to intake: look for splits, loose clamps and oil mist.

causes.name: Wastegate or vane actuator stuck
causes.why: The actuator sets how much exhaust drives the turbine. Stuck one way gives little boost; stuck the other gives too much and the computer cuts power.
signs: Power cuts suddenly under hard acceleration, then returns after a restart

causes.name: Boost control solenoid or vacuum line fault
causes.why: The computer moves the actuator through a solenoid, often by vacuum. A failed solenoid or a split pipe leaves the actuator uncontrolled.
signs: Boost fault that comes and goes
checks: Look at the small vacuum pipes near the turbo for cracks or one that has come off.

causes.name: Damaged compressor wheel
causes.why: Bent or chipped blades, usually from something drawn in past a poor filter, move less air and make noise.
signs: A loud siren that rises with engine speed

causes.name: Damaged turbine or worn shaft bearings
causes.why: Worn bearings let the shaft wobble until the wheels touch their housings; seals then pass oil.

causes.name: Oil starvation of the turbo
causes.why: The shaft spins on a film of engine oil. Low oil, a blocked feed pipe or dirty oil destroys the bearings quickly.
signs: Turbo failed soon after an overdue oil change
checks: Check the engine oil level and its condition.

causes.name: Supercharger not delivering
causes.why: A slipping drive belt, a clutch that does not engage or a bypass valve stuck open means the supercharger adds little air.
checks: Look at the supercharger drive belt for glazing and slack.

causes.name: Fuel delivery problem
causes.why: If the pressure or volume of fuel is too low, the injectors cannot supply what the engine asks for, most of all under load.
checks: Is there fuel in the tank, and is it the right fuel?
Switch the ignition on and listen for the pump humming for a moment from the rear of the car.

causes.name: Clogged fuel filter
causes.why: The filter traps dirt and water. As it fills, flow drops first at high demand.
signs: Cuts out or hesitates under sustained load

causes.name: Weak in-tank fuel pump
causes.why: A worn pump keeps the engine running at idle but cannot hold pressure when demand rises.
signs: Worse with a low tank or when hot

causes.name: High-pressure pump fault
causes.why: A diesel needs very high rail pressure to atomise fuel. A worn high-pressure pump cannot reach it; it can also shed metal into the system.

causes.name: Fuel pressure sensor or regulator fault
causes.why: The computer controls rail pressure from a sensor and a regulator. A wrong reading or a sticking regulator gives the wrong pressure.
signs: Stalling when coming to a stop

causes.name: Wrong or contaminated fuel
causes.why: Water, stale fuel or the wrong fuel type burns poorly and can damage pumps and injectors.
signs: Trouble began just after filling up
checks: Did the problem start straight after refuelling? If the wrong fuel may have gone in, do not run the engine.

causes.name: Ignition problem
causes.why: A weak or missing spark leaves the fuel in that cylinder unburned, so it adds little or no power.
signs: Engine warning light flashing under load
checks: Does the engine shake more at idle or under load? A flashing engine light means misfires are being counted.

causes.name: Worn or fouled spark plugs
causes.why: The gap widens and the electrodes round off with use, so the spark gets weaker; oil or soot can short it out.

causes.name: Failed ignition coil
causes.why: A coil that breaks down, often when hot, leaves one cylinder without spark.
signs: A steady misfire on one cylinder

causes.name: Coil connector or wiring damage
causes.why: A cracked connector or chafed wire interrupts the signal to a coil.
signs: Misfire that changes when the loom is moved

causes.name: Fuel injector problem
causes.why: A blocked injector delivers too little fuel and a leaking one too much; either upsets that cylinder.

causes.name: Clogged injector
causes.why: Deposits narrow the nozzle, so the spray is weak and uneven.

causes.name: Leaking or over-fuelling injector
causes.why: An injector that does not close fully drips fuel into the cylinder; the mixture goes rich and fuel can wash oil from the bore.

causes.name: Injector wiring or driver fault
causes.why: The injector is fine but is not being opened correctly.

causes.name: Glow plug fault
causes.why: A diesel ignites fuel by the heat of compression. When cold, glow plugs add the missing heat; if they fail, a cold engine cranks for a long time and smokes white before it catches.
signs: White smoke and rough running for the first seconds

causes.name: Intake air leak
causes.why: Air entering after the air meter is not accounted for, so the mixture runs lean, mostly at idle.
checks: Listen around the intake for a hiss at idle and look for a split or loose hose.

causes.name: EGR valve stuck or clogged
causes.why: Stuck open, it feeds exhaust gas into the intake when the engine needs fresh air: hesitation, rough idle and smoke. Stuck closed mainly raises emissions.

causes.name: Engine sensor fault
causes.why: The engine computer meters fuel, boost and timing from its sensors. A wrong reading makes it supply the wrong amounts, and a detected fault can trigger reduced-power mode.
checks: Have the stored fault codes read; they name the sensor circuit involved.

causes.name: Air mass sensor dirty or failed
causes.why: If the sensor under-reads the incoming air, the computer injects too little fuel and limits boost.
signs: Flat acceleration with no obvious misfire

causes.name: Oxygen sensor fault
causes.why: The sensor tells the computer whether the mixture is rich or lean. A slow or wrong sensor makes it correct the wrong way.

causes.name: Crankshaft position sensor fault
causes.why: Without a clean crankshaft signal the computer cannot time injection or spark. The engine may cut out when hot or refuse to start.
signs: Cuts out when hot, restarts once cooled
Rev counter does not move while cranking
checks: Watch the rev counter while cranking: no movement at all is a clue.

causes.name: Throttle body dirty or failing
causes.why: Carbon around the throttle plate, or a failing motor or position sensor, upsets the air supply at idle and the response to the pedal.
signs: Stalls when coming to a stop

causes.name: Blocked catalytic converter or exhaust
causes.why: A melted or broken-up catalyst core blocks the exhaust; the engine cannot expel its gas and power fades as revs rise.
signs: Power falls away at higher revs
A rattle from under the car

causes.name: Catalyst damaged by unburned fuel
causes.why: A long-running misfire sends unburned fuel into the converter, where it burns and melts the core. The misfire is the real cause.
signs: A history of misfires or a flashing engine light

causes.name: Diesel particulate filter blocked
causes.why: A filter loaded with soot restricts the exhaust, so the engine cannot breathe out; the computer then limits power.
checks: Has the car been used mostly for short trips? Has a DPF warning been showing?

causes.name: Regeneration never completes (short trips)
causes.why: Burning off the soot needs sustained exhaust heat. Repeated short, cold journeys interrupt it every time.
signs: Warning clears after a long run

causes.name: Regeneration prevented by another fault
causes.why: The computer will not start a regeneration while certain faults are present: a faulty EGR valve, injector, glow plug or sensor, or a thermostat stuck open.
signs: Other warning lights or stored codes

causes.name: Differential pressure sensor or its hoses
causes.why: The computer judges how full the filter is from the pressure across it. A failed sensor or a split hose makes a clean filter look blocked, or the reverse.
signs: Warning returns straight after a regeneration

causes.name: Filter full of ash
causes.why: Ash from burnt oil does not burn off. Over a long life it fills the filter and regeneration no longer clears it.

causes.name: AdBlue system fault
causes.why: If the fluid is low, of poor quality, or the dosing system or NOx sensors fail, the computer warns and may eventually prevent a restart.
signs: AdBlue warning with a distance countdown
checks: Check the AdBlue level and any countdown message.

causes.name: Reduced-power (limp) mode
causes.why: When the computer detects a fault that could cause damage it limits power on purpose. The stored fault code points to the real cause.
signs: Sudden loss of power with a warning light
Normal again after a restart, then it returns
checks: Have the stored fault codes read: they identify which system triggered it.

causes.name: Low compression (engine wear)
causes.why: Worn rings, leaking valves or a failed gasket let pressure escape from a cylinder, so less of the fuel's energy pushes the piston.
signs: Uneven idle that no ignition or fuel part cures
Oil consumption, breathing from the oil filler
checks: A workshop compression or leak-down test measures this directly.

causes.name: Worn piston rings or bores
causes.why: Rings that no longer seal let combustion pressure past into the crankcase and let oil up into the cylinder.

causes.name: Leaking or burnt valve
causes.why: A valve that does not seat lets pressure escape into the intake or exhaust.
signs: A regular puffing in the exhaust note

causes.name: Worn valve stem seals
causes.why: Hardened seals let oil run down the valve stems into the cylinders, mostly while the engine stands or idles.
signs: A puff of blue smoke on start-up or after idling

causes.name: Valve timing out (stretched chain or slipped belt)
causes.why: If the camshafts are out of step with the crankshaft, valves open at the wrong moment: power drops, the engine runs rough, and in the worst case valves meet pistons.
checks: A rattle for the first seconds after a cold start is worth reporting to a workshop promptly.

causes.name: Crankcase ventilation fault
causes.why: A blocked or split breather lets crankcase pressure push oil mist into the intake, or lets unmetered air in.

causes.name: Turbocharger passing oil
causes.why: Worn turbo bearings and seals let engine oil into the intake or exhaust, where it burns.

causes.name: Engine oil overfilled
causes.why: Too much oil is whipped up by the crankshaft and forced into the breather, where it is burned.
signs: Level above MAX on the dipstick
checks: Check the level on level ground with the engine off for a few minutes.

causes.name: Normal condensation
causes.why: On a cold start, water vapour in the exhaust condenses and shows as thin white vapour that disappears once everything is warm. That is normal.
signs: No smell, gone after a few minutes

causes.name: Weak or discharged 12 V battery
causes.why: The starter needs a very high current. An old, discharged or cold battery cannot hold its voltage under that load, so the engine turns slowly or only clicks. Electric and hybrid cars also need the 12 V battery to wake up.
checks: Note whether cranking is slower than usual, especially when cold.
Look at the terminals for white or green corrosion and loose clamps.
A parts shop or workshop can load-test the battery.

causes.name: Battery at the end of its life
causes.why: Capacity fades with age and with every deep discharge until the battery can no longer deliver starting current.

causes.name: Corroded or loose terminals or earth strap
causes.why: A poor connection adds resistance exactly where the largest current flows.
signs: Everything dies when the starter is tried, then comes back
checks: Look at both terminals and try to twist the clamps by hand: they should not move.

causes.name: Battery not being charged
causes.why: If the alternator does not charge, the battery runs everything until it is empty.
checks: Is the battery warning light on with the engine running?

causes.name: Alternator failed
causes.why: Worn brushes, a failed regulator or diodes stop it producing current.
signs: Whine or grinding from the alternator

causes.name: Auxiliary belt slipping or broken
causes.why: The alternator is belt-driven. A slack, glazed or broken belt stops it charging; on many engines the same belt drives the water pump and power steering.
signs: Squeal on start-up or when turning the wheel
Heavy steering and rising temperature at the same time
checks: Look at the belt for cracks, fraying and glazing.

causes.name: Charging cable, fuse or earth fault
causes.why: The alternator produces current but it does not reach the battery.

causes.name: DC/DC converter not charging the 12 V battery
causes.why: Electric and hybrid cars charge the 12 V battery from the traction battery through a converter instead of an alternator. If it fails the 12 V battery runs flat.
signs: 12 V battery warning on an electric or hybrid car

causes.name: Something draining the battery while parked
causes.why: A control unit that does not go to sleep, an accessory wired to permanent power or a light left on empties the battery over hours or days.
signs: Flat after standing, fine after a jump start and a long drive
checks: Was anything fitted recently (dash cam, tracker, stereo)? Is a boot or glovebox light staying on?

causes.name: Too many short trips
causes.why: Each start takes more out of the battery than a few minutes of driving put back.
signs: Mostly short journeys, many electrical loads

causes.name: Starter motor problem
causes.why: The starter turns the engine through a small gear that engages the flywheel. A worn motor, a failed solenoid or damaged teeth mean the engine is not turned properly.
signs: One loud click and no cranking
checks: Do the dashboard lights stay bright when the key is turned? Bright lights with no cranking point away from the battery and towards the starter.

causes.name: Starter solenoid failed
causes.why: The solenoid both pushes the gear into mesh and switches the heavy current. If its contacts are burnt it clicks but the motor does not turn.

causes.name: Worn starter motor
causes.why: Worn brushes or bearings make the motor weak or intermittent.
signs: Slow cranking with a known-good battery

causes.name: Damaged flywheel ring gear
causes.why: Missing or worn teeth where the starter engages: the starter spins or grinds at that spot.
signs: Starts after the engine is nudged round

causes.name: Starter cable or relay fault
causes.why: No current, or too little, reaches the starter.
signs: Nothing at all when the key is turned, lights unaffected

causes.name: Immobiliser or key not recognised
causes.why: If the car does not recognise the key, the computer blocks fuel or the starter by design.
signs: Key or padlock symbol on the dashboard
checks: Try the spare key. A flat key-fob battery can also stop keyless cars recognising it.

causes.name: Start interlock not satisfied
causes.why: Most cars refuse to start unless the selector is in Park or Neutral, or the clutch or brake pedal is pressed. A failed switch gives the same result.
signs: Starts in Neutral but not in Park
checks: Press the brake or clutch firmly and try Neutral as well as Park. Do the brake lights work?

causes.name: High-voltage system will not switch on
causes.why: An electric or hybrid car closes its contactors only after its self-checks pass. A detected fault, an isolation warning or a very low traction battery blocks it.
signs: A warning message instead of READY
No click from under the car when switching on
checks: Note the exact warning message; it usually names the system.

causes.name: Traction battery empty or very cold
causes.why: Below a minimum charge or temperature the battery management system will not allow the car to drive.

causes.name: Isolation or interlock fault
causes.why: The car continuously checks that the high-voltage circuit is insulated from the body and that every connector is seated. Any doubt keeps the system off.
checks: Do not open or touch orange high-voltage cables or components. This needs a trained technician.

causes.name: Low engine oil level
causes.why: With too little oil the pump draws air, pressure collapses and the bearings lose their protective film.
signs: Level below MIN on the dipstick
Warning flickers in corners or under braking
checks: On level ground with the engine off for a few minutes, check the dipstick or the electronic level display.

causes.name: External oil leak
causes.why: Oil escapes through a hardened gasket or seal.
signs: Oily, dirty patches on the engine
checks: Look under the car where it is parked and around the engine for wet oil.

causes.name: Valve cover gasket
causes.why: The gasket at the top of the engine hardens with heat and lets oil run down the outside.
signs: Oil on the side of the head, burning-oil smell from the exhaust manifold

causes.name: Sump gasket or drain plug
causes.why: The seal of the oil pan, or the drain plug and its washer, weeps oil at the lowest point of the engine.
signs: Drips from the very bottom of the engine

causes.name: Oil filter or its housing seal
causes.why: A filter that is loose, double-gasketed or has a hardened housing seal leaks under pressure.
signs: Leak began after an oil change

causes.name: Crankshaft oil seals
causes.why: The seals where the crankshaft leaves the block harden and leak; the rear one drips between engine and gearbox.
signs: Oil at the joint between engine and gearbox

causes.name: Engine burning oil
causes.why: Oil reaches the combustion chamber past rings, valve seals or the turbo, and is burned.

causes.name: Worn oil pump or blocked pickup
causes.why: A worn pump or a pickup strainer blocked with sludge cannot supply enough oil, most noticeably hot at idle.
signs: Warning at hot idle that clears with revs

causes.name: Blocked oil filter or overdue oil
causes.why: An overdue filter restricts flow, and old oil thins out and carries sludge.
checks: When was the oil last changed?

causes.name: Oil pressure sensor or wiring fault
causes.why: A failed sender or a chafed wire switches the warning on although pressure is fine. It must never be assumed.
signs: Warning with a quiet engine and a correct oil level
checks: Treat the warning as real until a workshop has measured the pressure with a gauge.

causes.name: Worn engine bearings
causes.why: Wide bearing clearances let oil escape too easily, so pressure cannot build; the bearings knock under load.
signs: Deep knocking that follows engine speed

causes.name: Knock from fuel or ignition (pinking)
causes.why: Fuel that ignites too early or on its own knocks against the rising piston. Low-grade fuel, heavy deposits or a failed knock sensor are typical reasons.
signs: Light metallic rattle under load that eases when you lift off
checks: Is the fuel grade the one the handbook asks for?

causes.name: Valve train tick
causes.why: A hydraulic tappet that does not pump up, or wear in the cam followers, ticks at half engine speed.
signs: Light ticking from the top of the engine, often worse cold

causes.name: Normal injector noise
causes.why: Direct-injection and diesel injectors click audibly as they work. A steady, even ticking that has always been there is normal.
signs: Even ticking at idle, unchanged for years

causes.name: Loose heat shield
causes.why: Thin metal shields around the exhaust corrode at their fixings and rattle at certain engine speeds.
signs: A tinny rattle at one particular rev range

causes.name: Worn engine mounts
causes.why: The rubber mounts isolate the engine. When they collapse or split, vibration and thumps reach the body.
signs: Thump when pulling away or changing gear
Vibration at idle that eases in neutral

causes.name: Exhaust leak
causes.why: Gas escaping before the silencers is loud, and near the engine it can also upset the oxygen sensor readings.
signs: Ticking or blowing that is loudest cold
checks: Look along the exhaust for soot streaks at joints and for holes.

causes.name: Cracked manifold or failed manifold gasket
causes.why: Heat cycles crack the manifold or burn out its gasket.
signs: Ticking on a cold start that fades as it warms

causes.name: Broken flexible section or joint
causes.why: The braided flexible section fatigues and splits; clamps and gaskets at joints corrode.
signs: Blowing from under the front of the car

causes.name: Corroded silencer or pipe
causes.why: Condensation rusts silencers from the inside, especially on cars used for short trips.

causes.name: Transmission not passing the power on
causes.why: If the clutch slips or an automatic does not hold its gear, engine speed rises without the car accelerating to match.
signs: Revs climb but speed does not

causes.name: Worn clutch plate
causes.why: The friction lining wears thin until the plate can no longer grip under full torque.
signs: Slips in high gears under full throttle
Biting point very high on the pedal
checks: In a high gear at low revs, accelerate firmly: if the revs rise without the car pulling, the clutch is slipping.

causes.name: Oil on the clutch
causes.why: A leaking crankshaft or gearbox seal lets oil reach the friction plate, which then slips and judders.
signs: Slipping on a clutch that is not old

causes.name: Clutch hydraulics or cable
causes.why: Air, a leak or a failing cylinder means the pedal no longer moves the clutch fully: it drags and gears baulk, or it does not release at all.
signs: Pedal soft, low or slow to return
Hard to select first or reverse when stationary
checks: Look at the clutch or brake fluid reservoir level.

causes.name: Weak pressure plate or worn dual-mass flywheel
causes.why: A tired pressure plate clamps too lightly; a worn dual-mass flywheel rattles and judders.
signs: Rattle at idle that changes with the clutch pedal

causes.name: Low or wrong gearbox oil
causes.why: Without the right oil the synchronisers cannot match speeds, so gears baulk and crunch.
signs: Notchy change that is worse cold

causes.name: Worn synchronisers
causes.why: The synchroniser rings wear and can no longer bring a gear up to speed before it engages.

causes.name: Worn gear linkage or cables
causes.why: Play in the linkage means the lever moves without fully selecting the gear.

causes.name: Low or degraded transmission fluid
causes.why: An automatic uses its fluid to apply clutches and to cool. Low or worn-out fluid gives slipping, delayed and harsh shifts.
signs: Dark fluid with a burnt smell
checks: Look under the car for red or brown fluid.

causes.name: Torque converter fault
causes.why: The lock-up clutch inside the converter can shudder or fail to lock, and the converter can lose efficiency.
signs: Shudder at a steady speed, like driving over rumble strips

causes.name: Shift solenoid, valve body or mechatronic fault
causes.why: Solenoids and valves direct the fluid that changes gear. When one sticks, particular shifts become harsh, slow or missing.
signs: Stuck in one gear with a warning
Harsh change between two particular gears

causes.name: Transmission adaptation or software
causes.why: The control unit learns clutch fill times. After a battery change, a repair or a fault, shifts can feel wrong until it relearns or is updated.
signs: Began after battery disconnection or a repair

causes.name: Worn CV joint
causes.why: The joint lets the driveshaft turn while the wheel steers and moves. Once worn it clicks on full lock under power.
signs: Rhythmic clicking in tight turns that speeds up with the car
checks: Look behind the front wheels at the rubber boots on the driveshafts: a split boot with grease thrown around is the usual start.

causes.name: Torn CV boot
causes.why: A split boot throws out the grease and lets in grit, which wears the joint quickly.
signs: Grease on the inside of the wheel and suspension

causes.name: Worn inner driveshaft joint
causes.why: The inner joint lets the shaft change length. When worn it shudders under acceleration and eases when coasting.

causes.name: Differential or final-drive wear
causes.why: Worn gears or bearings, or low oil, make the final drive whine or hum, changing between drive and overrun.
signs: Whine that changes when you lift off
checks: Look for oil on the differential casing.

causes.name: Propshaft joint or centre bearing
causes.why: A worn universal joint or centre bearing lets the shaft run out of true.
signs: Vibration through the floor that rises with road speed

causes.name: Uneven brake disc ("warped" disc)
causes.why: If the disc's thickness varies around its circumference, the pads are pushed back and forth every turn. You feel it as a pulsing pedal and a shaking steering wheel.
signs: Pedal pulses in time with wheel speed
Worse from high speed and when hot
checks: Does the vibration appear only while braking, and grow with speed?

causes.name: Uneven pad material on the disc
causes.why: Holding the brakes on hard after a hot stop prints pad material onto the disc in patches; the grip then varies around the disc.
signs: Bluish or patchy marks on the disc

causes.name: Sticking brake caliper
causes.why: A seized piston or slider keeps a pad rubbing. That corner runs hot, the disc wears unevenly and the car may pull.
signs: One wheel much hotter than the others
More brake dust on one wheel
checks: After a drive without heavy braking, carefully sense the heat coming off each wheel without touching: one much hotter stands out.

causes.name: Wheel hub runout or bearing play
causes.why: If the hub face is not true, or the bearing has play, the disc wobbles as it turns.
signs: New discs start to vibrate again after a short time

causes.name: Play in suspension or steering joints
causes.why: Worn joints and bushes do not create the vibration, but they let a small one shake the whole wheel, and they let the wheel change direction under braking.

causes.name: Brake pads worn out
causes.why: A wear indicator squeals when the friction material is nearly gone. After that the steel backing grinds on the disc and braking is badly reduced.
checks: Look through the wheel at the pad: there should be clearly visible friction material between its backing plate and the disc.

causes.name: Glazed or poor-quality pads
causes.why: Overheated pads develop a hard, shiny surface that squeals and grips less.
signs: Squeal with plenty of pad left

causes.name: Scored, rusty or lipped disc
causes.why: Grooves, a rust band after standing, or a raised lip at the edge make noise as the pad passes.
signs: Noise after the car has stood in the wet

causes.name: Missing or seized pad hardware
causes.why: Shims, clips and sliders let the pad sit and move correctly. Without them it vibrates and squeals.
signs: Squeal began after pads were changed

causes.name: Stone or debris behind the disc
causes.why: A small stone between the disc and its shield scrapes continuously.
signs: A constant metallic scraping, braking or not

causes.name: Air in the brake lines
causes.why: Brake fluid cannot be compressed; air can. With air in the lines the pedal travel goes into squeezing bubbles instead of the pads.
checks: Does pumping the pedal twice make it higher and firmer?

causes.name: Low brake fluid
causes.why: The level falls slowly as pads wear, and quickly if there is a leak. If it gets low enough, air is drawn in.
checks: Compare the level in the brake fluid reservoir with its MIN and MAX marks.

causes.name: Brake fluid leak
causes.why: A corroded pipe, a perished hose or a leaking caliper or cylinder seal lets fluid out and air in.
signs: Wet patch inside a wheel or under the car
checks: Look at the inside of each wheel and under the car for fluid.

causes.name: Old brake fluid (boiling)
causes.why: Brake fluid absorbs moisture over the years, which lowers its boiling point. Under hard use it boils and the vapour compresses like air.
signs: Pedal goes soft after repeated heavy braking, recovers when cool

causes.name: Master cylinder failing
causes.why: Worn seals inside let fluid slip past the piston, so the pedal sinks slowly under steady pressure.
signs: Pedal creeps to the floor at a standstill

causes.name: Flexible hose swelling or collapsed
causes.why: An aged hose balloons under pressure (soft pedal), or collapses inside and holds pressure on one brake (pull, drag).

causes.name: Wheel speed sensor fault
causes.why: ABS and stability control compare the speed of each wheel. A failed sensor, damaged wiring or a cracked sensor ring switches them off.
signs: ABS cutting in at walking pace

causes.name: ABS pump or control unit fault
causes.why: The hydraulic unit or its electronics have failed their self-test.
signs: ABS light with no sensor fault stored

causes.name: Dragging brake
causes.why: A caliper or handbrake that does not release holds the car back and heats that wheel.
signs: One wheel much hotter than the others

causes.name: Handbrake not releasing
causes.why: A seized cable or an electric parking brake actuator that does not retract keeps the rear brakes on.

causes.name: Wrong or uneven tyre pressure
causes.why: A soft tyre has more rolling resistance and less grip than its opposite number, so the car pulls towards it, steers heavily and uses more energy.
checks: Check all four pressures cold against the figures on the door-pillar label.

causes.name: Wheel alignment out
causes.why: If the wheels do not point where they should, the car drifts and the tyres wear on one edge.
signs: Steering wheel off-centre on a straight road
checks: Look at the front tyres: is one edge worn more than the other?

causes.name: Uneven or damaged tyres
causes.why: A tyre with uneven wear, a bulge, a flat spot or an internal fault pulls, vibrates or drones.
signs: Noise changes with the road surface
checks: Run a hand over the tread (car parked): scalloped or stepped blocks can be felt.

causes.name: Wheel out of balance
causes.why: A wheel and tyre that are heavier on one side shake at a particular speed, usually motorway speed.
signs: Shake in a narrow speed band, smooth above and below
A balance weight missing from the rim

causes.name: Bent or damaged wheel
causes.why: A rim bent by a pothole or kerb runs out of true.

causes.name: Worn wheel bearing
causes.why: A worn bearing hums or rumbles, louder with speed and changing when the car's weight shifts in a bend.
signs: Hum that changes when you steer gently left and right at speed
checks: On a clear road at steady speed, steer gently one way then the other: a noise that comes and goes with direction suggests a bearing.

causes.name: Worn suspension bushes
causes.why: Rubber bushes locate the suspension arms. When they split or soften, the arm moves and knocks.
signs: Clunk when braking or pulling away

causes.name: Worn ball joint
causes.why: The ball joint is the pivot between the arm and the hub. Play in it knocks and affects steering; a failed one is dangerous.

causes.name: Worn track rod end
causes.why: Play in the joint that connects the steering rack to the wheel makes the steering vague and lets the wheel shake.
signs: Free play at the steering wheel

causes.name: Worn anti-roll bar links or bushes
causes.why: The small links that join the bar to the suspension are the commonest source of a light knock over uneven surfaces.
signs: Light rattle over small bumps at low speed

causes.name: Worn dampers
causes.why: A damper that has lost its oil or gas no longer controls the spring: the car bounces, and the unit can knock.
signs: Oil misting on the damper body
Car keeps bouncing after a bump
checks: Look at each damper for an oily film.

causes.name: Worn strut top mount
causes.why: The mount and its bearing at the top of a front strut wear; they knock over bumps and creak when steering.
signs: Creak or twang when turning the wheel at a standstill

causes.name: Broken coil spring
causes.why: A spring that has snapped, usually at its end coil, lets that corner sit low and knock.
signs: A bang, then a new noise
checks: Compare the gap between tyre and wheel arch side to side.

causes.name: Power steering assistance lost
causes.why: Without assistance the steering still works but needs far more effort, most of all when parking.

causes.name: Low power steering fluid (hydraulic systems)
causes.why: A hydraulic system needs its fluid to transmit assistance. A leak lets the level fall and the pump draws air.
signs: Fluid under the front of the car
checks: If the car has a power steering reservoir, compare its level with the marks.

causes.name: Electric power steering fault
causes.why: An electric system depends on its motor, torque sensor and a healthy electrical supply. A fault or low voltage switches the assistance off.

causes.name: Steering rack or column binding
causes.why: A dry or damaged rack, or a seizing column joint, makes the steering stiff or notchy and slow to self-centre.
signs: Stiff spots, does not return to centre by itself

causes.name: Low refrigerant
causes.why: The system cools by evaporating refrigerant. With too little, it cannot absorb enough heat, and the compressor may be switched off to protect it.
signs: Colder while driving than at idle
Compressor clicks on and off rapidly

causes.name: Refrigerant leak
causes.why: Refrigerant escapes through a stone-damaged condenser, a hardened seal or a porous hose. Some loss over many years is normal; a fast loss is a leak.
signs: Works after a recharge, then fades again

causes.name: Compressor not running
causes.why: If the compressor or its clutch does not engage, or its drive belt slips, no refrigerant is pumped.
signs: No change in engine note when the A/C is switched on

causes.name: Condenser blocked or damaged
causes.why: The condenser sheds the heat taken from the cabin. Blocked fins or a failed fan stop it doing so.
signs: Cold on the move, warm in traffic
checks: Look through the grille at the condenser fins for debris and damage.

causes.name: Clogged cabin filter
causes.why: A blocked pollen filter chokes the airflow, so little cooled or heated air reaches the cabin.

causes.name: Blower motor or its control
causes.why: If the fan that pushes air through the vents fails, or its speed control does, there is little or no airflow.

causes.name: A/C fuse, relay or pressure sensor
causes.why: The system will not run if its pressure sensor, relay or fuse has failed.
signs: A/C light on but nothing happens

causes.name: Battery limiting power
causes.why: The battery management system reduces the power it allows when the cells are very cold, very hot or nearly empty, to protect them.
signs: Power-limit symbol or a shortened power gauge
After fast charging, hard driving or a freezing night
checks: Note the battery temperature and charge level when it happens.

causes.name: Inverter or motor fault
causes.why: The inverter turns battery power into the alternating current the motor needs. If either overheats or detects a fault, drive power is cut back or stopped.
signs: Whine or shudder from the drive unit

causes.name: Drive electronics cooling fault
causes.why: The inverter and motor have their own coolant circuit and electric pump. Low coolant or a failed pump makes them overheat.
signs: Power cut after sustained hard driving

causes.name: Traction battery capacity loss
causes.why: Every battery loses capacity with age, charge cycles and heat. Less capacity means less range and less peak power.
signs: Full charge shows less range than when new

causes.name: Cold weather
causes.why: Cold cells deliver less energy, and heating the cabin and the battery takes a share of it. Range in winter is noticeably lower without anything being wrong.

causes.name: Speed, load and climate use
causes.why: Air resistance rises steeply with speed; heavy loads, roof boxes and heating or cooling all draw from the same battery.
signs: Range estimate falls fastest on fast roads

causes.name: Battery heating or cooling fault
causes.why: The pack is kept in its working temperature range by its own circuit. If that fails the pack runs too hot or cold, and charging and power are limited.

causes.name: Charging cable or charging point
causes.why: The fault may not be in the car: a damaged cable, a tripped supply or a faulty public charger stops the session.
signs: Works on a different charger or cable
checks: Try another charging point or cable before suspecting the car.

causes.name: Charge port or its lock
causes.why: Bent or dirty contacts, or a locking pin that does not engage, stop the car and charger agreeing to start.
signs: Port light flashing a fault colour
checks: Look into the port for debris, moisture or bent pins. Do not poke inside it.

causes.name: On-board charger fault
causes.why: The on-board charger converts AC from the socket to DC for the battery. If it fails, AC charging stops while DC rapid charging may still work.
signs: Home (AC) charging fails, rapid (DC) charging works

causes.name: Charge timer or limit set
causes.why: A scheduled-charging timer, a charge limit or a departure setting can make the car wait instead of charging.
signs: Stops at the same percentage each time
checks: Look in the charging menu for a schedule or limit.
